RAG Test Document
This document is intentionally created for testing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline. It
contains factual information that can later beretrieved by a vector database and used by an LLM.
1. What is RAG?
Retrieval-Augmented Generation, commonly called RAG, is a technique that combines information
retrieval with text generation. Instead of relying only on information learned during model training, a RAG

When a user asks a question, the question can first be converted into an embedding. The retriever then
searches the vector store and returns the most relevant document chunks. These retrieved chunks
become context for the language model.
7. Generation
The language model receives the user's question together with the retrieved context. It uses that context
to generate an answer. A well-designed RAG system should answer using the retrieved information
rather than inventing unsupported facts.
